sentences: Complementation replaces a finite automaton's language by the set of words it rejects.
Starting from an unambiguous automaton, the project asks how large a nondeterministic automaton for the complement must become.
The source particularly seeks to close the gap for binary and larger alphabets, where its upper bound remains exponential.
Unique accepting runs simplify the original language without automatically providing short certificates of rejection.
Tight conversion bounds would quantify the representation cost of negating specifications whose positive witnesses are unambiguous.
